💡 Key Takeaways
  • Landon Tresp, 16, left, met the girl playing Among Us before alerting his mother, Khristina, 41, to the missing teen's predicament.
  • Sixteen-year-old Landon Tresp was in the bedroom of his family's Colorado mountain home, playing an online game after finishing his daily chores, when he began chatting on his laptop with another player.
  • She was also a teenager, and the pair "kind of just clicked," he tells the BBC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Landon Tresp, 16, left, met the girl playing Among Us before alerting his mother, Khristina, 41, to the missing teen's predicament.

Sixteen-year-old Landon Tresp was in the bedroom of his family's Colorado mountain home, playing an online game after finishing his daily chores, when he began chatting on his laptop with another player.

She was also a teenager, and the pair "kind of just clicked," he tells the BBC.

According to recent reports, he told her he liked her name, and she confessed that it was an alias. She was a runaway, she remarked - and was being held against her will, hundreds of miles from home, though she didn't know exactly where. The girl, 17, and had been missing for more than a year.

In a recent development, stunned, Landon felt "helpless," he states - and, after learning more details over two weeks of chatting, he decided to tell his mother, Khristina on 31 October this year. The 41-year-old nurse and mother of five was putting Halloween makeup on her younger children for trick-or-treating when he briefed her.

That set the mother and son on a path to track down his friend, contact her mother, cooperate with the FBI - and ultimately witness the rescue of the teen - only 24 hours after Landon first alerted Khristina to her plight.

"She had one opportunity to reach out her hand and ask for help, and she chose me," Khristina indicates of the girl, who was 15 when she went missing.

A screenshot highlights Khristina on a call with the girl as she showed her the knife her alleged captor kept under his pillow.

The Tresps have shared with BBC screenshots of communication with the girl and a photo matching the criminal complaint to corroborate their story.

Landon first told his mother about "Jenny" - whose identity the BBC is protecting - in mid-October, a few weeks before the rescue.

"He had mentioned something about maybe a week or so into talking to her that he met a girl online, and she was really sweet," notes Khristina - who cautioned him that "you don't always know who's on the other side of the screen".

"She's just having a really hard time and looking for a friend," he told her.

But Landon was becoming increasingly concerned as Jenny told him more about her situation.

They'd met playing Among Us, a game Landon describes as "kind of like online space Clue".

Recent findings suggest that after telling Landon that she was a runaway, "Jenny" stated an older man had taken her across state lines and wouldn't let her leave. She was the subject of a missing person investigation, and she sent Landon links to stories about her disappearance. But she believed police were no longer looking for her.

Jenny was scared and desperate, and that's why Landon went to his mother.

Her maternal instincts on high alert, Khristina contacted Jenny herself on Discord, the encrypted platform.

During the conversation, Khristina remarked she told the Colorado mother how she'd been through "years of abuse in her life and lots and lots of problems".

Within hours, Jenny started calling Khristina "mama".

Among Us supports cross platform play online with 4-15 players on various devices.

It has been revealed that the Colorado mother knew things were serious when she read the missing persons articles. Jenny knew she was in Oregon and gave the name of a city, but she didn't know where she was being held exactly. Khristina knew she needed more. She told Jenny to find a piece of mail or another document in the house that had a full name on it, which the girl did.

"That's when I went to work," Khristina says, delving into tax and property records.

Khristina narrowed down addresses, then searched them on a real estate site to find pictures. She showed the photos to Jenny, who confirmed that the second one was where she was being held.

The "next thing she asked me was to please not tell anyone until [her captor] was gone - that he did have weapons in the house and she was very scared," Khristina stated.

Jenny promised Khristina she'd call her back through the game platform when he left the next morning, and in the meantime Khristina began looking for the law enforcement agency that had been assigned to the missing teen's case. She contacted Jenny's mother on social media, spoke briefly to her on the phone and then got a call from an FBI agent.

"Have you seen her alive?'" the agent asked Khristina.

"And I said: 'I have; I video chatted with her, I've seen her, and she goes 'Oh my God, I cannot believe any of this'," Khristina recalled.

When Jenny called Khristina back after her alleged captor left home, the FBI monitored their conversation. According to the criminal complaint's record of the conversation, Jenny explained how she'd met Adam Hunter Harmel on social media in May 2025.

He'd told her he was disabled and his hips were "messed up," offering Jenny money if she'd help get him to Oregon.

After he picked her up in Utah, however, Harmel threw her phone into a river, drove her to Oregon and kept her in the basement. He forced her to sleep against the wall in his bed, with a knife under his pillow, to prevent her from escaping. He gave Jenny a cell phone with no ability to make calls, but it could connect to wifi, which is how she played the online game.

The 39-year-old "would become violent and aggressive", the document indicates, which included hitting her and sexually assaulting her.

He also allegedly forced Jenny to remove her braces with pliers so she wouldn't be identifiable.

As Khristina and the FBI heard all of this, law enforcement were staging to bring Jenny to safety, after being alerted to her whereabouts.

While Harmel was out of the home, officers were sent to the street and the address, and Khristina was prepping Jenny for her run to freedom.

She'd unsuccessfully tried escaping before, she told Khristina.

Law enforcement was "phenomenalâ¦giving me an update, you know, 'We're nine minutes out, we're seven minutes out,'" says Khristina, who was on the phone with Jenny the entire time, her son Landon watching at her side.

Khristina could hear other people in the home with Jenny, and she was afraid that someone would catch wind of what was happening and harm the girl.

But she kept any of those fears from Jenny.

Industry observers note that "I want you to take three deep breaths with me," she told the teen. "When an officer tells me to go, and I relay that message to you, I want you to run up those stairs as fast as you can â¦ Grab that basement door.

"I want you to keep going down that hallway and grab that front doorâ¦ do not stop.'".

The mother and son watched breathlessly as Jenny ran into the arms of a state trooper.

Industry observers note that harmel is now in federal custody and has been charged in a criminal complaint with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity. Local Oregon media also reported he'd been accused of sexually abusing a six-year-old in the months before Jenny disappeared - and a sexual abuse protective order was granted against him in March 2025.

He remains behind bars awaiting trial.

A lawyer for the defendant did not respond to a BBC request for comment.

Jenny, meanwhile, remains in daily communication with Khristina and Landon - who still enjoys playing online games with her.

According to recent reports, "Sometimes we just sit on video chat, just so she knows she has someone that cares," Khristina says. "She was on video last night when I cooked dinner â¦it's nice to know that when she has a bad day or a bad moment, she can call me right away or call Landon right away.".

"She's doing great for what she's gone through.".

They haven't met in person yet, but they're in the process of trying to make that happen.

"I hope I can put my arms around her soon," Khristina says.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the 4th-gen Apple TV 4K comes with a fresh remote.
  • Recent findings suggest that earlier this October, Apple unveiled its latest Apple TV 4K streaming box.
  • In a recent development, one of the most underrated aspects of the newly introduced Apple TV 4K is the introduction of its new remote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the 4th-gen Apple TV 4K comes with a fresh remote. Here's what you need to know about it.

Recent findings suggest that earlier this October, Apple unveiled its latest Apple TV 4K streaming box. Like most product rolls out in recent months, the release centered around a "supercharged" AI offering, which Apple believes will transform "how users search for, discover, and enjoy their favorite movies and TV highlights through a full-screen Siri AI experience." In its announcement, Apple touted the AI-enabled fourth generation of its popular streaming hub as the "most immersive home theater experience yet.".

In a recent development, one of the most underrated aspects of the newly introduced Apple TV 4K is the introduction of its new remote. At first glance, the Siri Remote doesn't appear much different. Sporting the same sleek silver and black design fashioned with 100 percent recycled aluminum, it retains the touch-enabled clickpad and voice recognition from its previous version. Like its third-generation predecessor, the new Siri Remote uses a USB-C port for quick recharging and better cross-compatibility.

However, the new Siri Remote builds on top of this beloved design by adding a more precise Find My feature. With Precision Finding, you can use your phone's Find My app to find exactly where your fourth-gen Siri Remote is hiding. The remote also adds the ability to play a sound when trying to locate it, much to the joy of those affected by the couch-swallowing gremlins plaguing America's living rooms.

Recent findings suggest that the new Apple TV 4K is now on available for purchase, and the new Siri Remote comes in the box. However, you will also be able purchase the fourth-generation Siri Remote separately via Apple's website or at your local Apple Store.

Retailing for $59, the remote is compatible with all four generations of the Apple TV 4K, as well as the Apple TV HD. Those holding onto Apple TV models from before 2015 will need to continue digging through their couch cushions.

This expanded compatibility is notable given Apple's plans for Siri AI. As it stands, the fine print of Apple's press release notes that the upcoming AI suite isn't exclusive to the new streaming box. Instead, the manufacturer is also pushing its Siri AI features to both Apple TV 4K's second- and third-generation boxes. So while you might be tempted to upgrade your streaming box in order to benefit from the faster speeds, an Ethernet port and a built-in microphones, you may also find that upgrading your Apple TV 4K simply isn't worth the $299 price tag. As such, you may want to consider simply upgrade your remote separately and save $240.

It has been revealed that there is a catch, however. In addition to a compatible streaming device, your fourth-gen Siri Remote will need to be paired with a relatively fresh iPhone to unlock its Precision Finding feature. As it stands, the feature is available to Apple viewers with an iPhone Duo, iPhone Air, or iPhone 17 or later, except the iPhone 17e. You will also need to run Apple's latest iOS software, iOS 27.

In a recent development, similar to people with a second- or third-generation Siri Remote, those with an older iPhone will be able to use Apple's Find My feature without Precision Finding. This may be a surprise, as Apple's iPhone 15 and 16 models support Precision Finding for products like the AirTag 2. However, some speculate that this is because Apple's Find My tech has transitioned from using its Ultra Wideband chip to Bluetooth 6 technology in this instance.

Apple promises that its Siri AI will make your Apple TV 4K more helpful and intuitive by adding a "profoundly more capable and conversational assistant with personal context understanding, broad world knowledge, and the ability to take even more systemwide app actions.".

In a recent development, siri AI allows you to ask your television questions like, "Siri, who won Best Comedy at this year's Emmy Awards?" You can also ask Siri questions about the film or show you are watching, such as filming locations, why recognize a particular actor or whether a movie is appropriate for your children. Responses are overlaid at the corner of your screen in order to not disrupt your viewing experience.

According to recent reports, in service of this mission, the box has three far-field microphones, extending your hands-free viewing experience across the room. Moreover, advanced echo cancellation allows your Apple TV 4K to isolate your voice and block out the noise, ensuring you don't spend half the show unsuccessfully screaming at Siri. This also means you don't have to speak all of your queries into the Siri Remote; the box itself can hear you.

Industry observers note that the new Apple TV 4K also promises significant speed gains. By adding a new A19 chip, Apple claims that its latest streaming box will achieve 50 percent faster CPU performance and up to twice the GPU speeds when compared to its third-gen predecessor. Its AV1 decoder will enable more bandwidth-efficient streams, increasing visual quality without overloading your network.

It has been revealed that connected to a four compatible HomePods, you can achieve Apple's best surround sound experience. Moreover, you can manage smart home hub notifications with AI-generated camera activity descriptions, doorbell notifications and enhanced control of select accessories.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Attorney general states E1 settlement decision should not be taken by caretaker government led by Netanyahu.

Israel has postponed issuing contracts for the construction of a large settlement on the West Bank seen as likely to render a two-state solution unviable, days after the UK imposed sanctions against building firms operating in the area.

Sources indicate that israeli diplomats insisted the move was not in response to the measures from Downing Street. Gali Baharav-Miara, the attorney general, mentioned any decision on settlement expansion should not be taken by the caretaker government led by Benjamin Netanyahu but by whatever newly introduced administration was formed.

She ordered the Israel land authority and ministry of housing not to open the tender process. Israeli diplomats suggested the UK foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, had acted prematurely on Monday in sanctioning the eight construction firms. But UK diplomats believe the growing political pressure on Israel over settlements, including from US Democrats, is having an impact.

It has been revealed that the deferral puts the E1 settlement expansion in the mix for any coalition negotiations. The leader of the Change bloc, Gadi Eisenkot, seen as Israel’s most likely next prime minister, has been clear in opposing violent settler activity, as has the newly elected Knesset speaker, Matan Kahana, an ally of Eisenkot.

Recent findings suggest that eisenkot has also opposed the E1 settlement expansion, describing it as a mistake likely to alienate international opinion. He said of the plan: “I recall that Netanyahu himself opposed this for a long time, and due to coalition pressure, he gave in and approved it.”.

The EI settlement expansion, due to have been announced on Thursday, has long been seen as qualitatively different since the land – between Jerusalem and Ma’aleh Adumim, a West Bank settlement city of nearly 40,000 residents – bisects the West Bank and cuts it off from East Jerusalem.

Miliband has noted it would mark the death knell of a future Palestinian state. The UK, along with a group of European countries, has recently recognised Palestine, and the preservation of a two-state solution has been described as the north star of Labour policy towards the region.

The construction tender was published for more than 3,401 housing units in the area. At the beginning of November, the Israel Defense Forces began demolishing homes in a Bedouin community within the E1 area.

Israel has already enforced the downgrading of the UK consulate in East Jerusalem as a reprisal for Miliband’s decision in September to try to end trade links with the illegal settlements.

Bennett mentioned: “The British Labour government’s hostility, bias and one-sided approach are particularly glaring given its failure to take any action against the Palestinian Authority, which continues to encourage terrorism through financial payments, promote incitement in its education system and engage in illegal construction in violation of signed agreements.”.

Although the Israeli election was largely fought on domestic security-related complications, Eisenkot seems to be more sensitive to the implications of Israel’s crumbling global reputation, and the need to make efforts to be seen to be listening to the criticism.

If he becomes prime minister, Eisenkot will, indirectly at least, also have to take account of the views of the Arab parties even if these parties are not going to become members of the government.

The group Peace Now welcomed the attorney general’s decision: “A government that lost the elections is not permitted to exploit its final days in power to advance destructive moves that will endanger Israel’s future and its international standing.

According to recent reports, construction in E1 is liable to eliminate the possibility of a two-state solution and drag Israel into a severe diplomatic crisis and international sanctions. The AG’s decision is an notable step, but the struggle is not over yet.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • United Nations talks on regulating lethal autonomous weapons systems ended on Saturday without an agreement on a legally binding ban.
  • The negotiations did, however, yield an agreement for further discussions to develop fresh rules by 2028.
  • Delegates from 128 states that are parties to the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) had been meeting in Geneva since Monday amid rising concerns over the use of the so-called killer robots in global conflicts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

United Nations talks on regulating lethal autonomous weapons systems ended on Saturday without an agreement on a legally binding ban.

The negotiations did, however, yield an agreement for further discussions to develop fresh rules by 2028.

Delegates from 128 states that are parties to the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) had been meeting in Geneva since Monday amid rising concerns over the use of the so-called killer robots in global conflicts.

The conference ended early on Saturday in what campaigners deemed a "weakened" outcome, following several hours of overnight parleying.

Nearly 100 nations had called for negotiations on a legally binding agreement on the systems capable of killing without a human making the final decision to fire.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres, Pope Leo XIV and the Red Cross had also supported a ban on killer robots.

However, countries that have the technology, including arms-producing giants like the ​US, Russia ‌and Israel, were among those opposing the mandate.

Ultimately, the 128 countries  "agreed to launch the elaboration of an international instrument on lethal autonomous weapons systems, which should be conducted over the next two years", the conference's Swiss chair, Julien Thoni, told the media on Saturday.

But while Thoni hailed a multilateral diplomacy delivering "concrete results" even in "today's deeply divided world," rights groups expressed disappointment at the minimal agreement.

"States adopted a watered-down mandate that fails to chart a clear path towards a legally binding instrument," news agency AFP quoted Stop Killer Robots, a global coalition of over 300 organizations, as saying.

Recent findings suggest that "Over 95 states expressed their support for a treaty. In the final hours, a small number of states weakened the mandate introducing uncertainty about the legal status of the final document," it added.

The group had earlier said that autonomous weapons systems were already reaching the battlefield and such systems had been tested or deployed, including in the Ukraine war.

Last week, DraftKings asked a federal court in Florida to take over a lawsuit recently filed against it by the Seminole Tribe, opening another front in the nationwide online “swaps” debate.

This Florida case adds to an already complex subplot involving Indigenous tribes, some of which are challenging prediction markets, while others are trying to get in on the action themselves.

In the new lawsuit, the Seminole Tribe contends that two of DraftKings’ current online offerings—the fantasy sports-style “Pick6” and the “Super App” sportsbook—are “illegal” in Florida.

The tribe argues that every such “wager that Defendants now accept through their illegal sportsbook siphons away revenue that funds both the Tribe’s and Florida’s public programs and government services.”.

Recent findings suggest that neither DraftKings nor its attorneys immediately responded to Ars’ request for comment. However, in a court filing, DraftKings indicates that its products available to Floridians are merely “fantasy sports and the trading of [financial] derivatives” and not gambling.

DraftKings notes that its “licensed sportsbook” operates in other states but “not in Florida.”.

Recent findings suggest that multiple companies, including DraftKings, claim that their “swaps” (a type of financial derivative) are, in fact, properly governed by a federal agency, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. Therefore, DraftKings argues, states cannot regulate this activity as gambling.

Industry observers note that the Seminoles, a sovereign nation and a federally recognized tribe, have a deal with the State of Florida, known as the 2021 Gaming Compact. That 30-year contract allows the tribe to maintain what the tribe states is the “exclusive right to offer online sports betting throughout the State of Florida.” In exchange, this betting regime is regulated, and Florida takes a cut.

But since that contract was signed, attorneys for the Seminole Tribe say in the complaint, DraftKings has pursued years of court challenges and a failed ballot measure designed to break into the Sunshine State.

As of 2026, DraftKings launched “Pick6” in Florida, a game where individuals can put money down while predicting specific outcomes—for example, whether Victor Wembanyama of the San Antonio Spurs will score more or less than 28.5 points in his next basketball game.

Industry observers note that “Based on DraftKings’ representations, Florida consumers may predictably but incorrectly conclude that Pick6 is a legal product in Florida. It is not,” the complaint states.

Sources indicate that “Pick6 is illegal ‘gambling’ under Florida law. DraftKings operates Pick6 without a license, without state oversight, and without any consumer protections Florida requires as a condition of legal sports wagering.”.

In June 2026, DraftKings launched what it calls a “Super App,” which the Seminole Tribe argues is a “one-stop shop for illegal gambling,” as it provides an interface that is “in the same format used by every traditional, regulated sportsbook.”.

Florida-based professor Robert Jarvis of Nova Southeastern University studies gambling law, and he told Ars by email that he didn’t “buy the argument” DraftKings put forward that its products cannot be regulated under Florida gambling law.

Jarvis also noted that the tribe caught a break, too, with their randomly assigned federal judge.

According to recent reports, “Not only have they had very good luck in federal court in previous cases, the federal judge assigned to the case is Ed Artau, who previously served as a Florida state trial judge (2014–20) and a Florida state appellate judge (2020–25),” he wrote. “Thus, in a sense, the Seminoles get the best of both worlds: a federal court run by a Florida state judge.”.

How to easily factory reset your Fitbit

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (714 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It can help fix a serious glitch or prep your wearable for a newly introduced owner.
  • If your Fitbit is acting up, you'll want to restart it, but this is a very different process from a factory reset.
  • There are only a few times you'll want to factory reset a Fitbit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It can help fix a serious glitch or prep your wearable for a newly introduced owner.

If your Fitbit is acting up, you'll want to restart it, but this is a very different process from a factory reset. You may want to restart your Fitbit if it won't sync with the Google Health app or isn't registering data. However, if the screen is unresponsive to taps or swipes, or it's frozen on a specific screen, you can force a hard restart, which typically involves pressing and holding a button (or buttons) for a specific period of time until the screen resets. How to restart your Fitbit device varies by model. It's a refresh, like turning something off and on again. A factory reset, on the other hand, removes all unsynced settings and data from the device and brings the wearable back to its original state when it was first purchased.

There are only a few times you'll want to factory reset a Fitbit. Do this if you're giving it to someone else or selling it. It's also worth doing for data privacy, if the device is no longer functioning properly and you're dropping it off for safe recycling. Finally, it's a last-ditch effort if a restart isn't fixing a major concern. Factory resetting your Fitbit is simple, but use this option only when necessary.

For Fitbits with a screen, go to Settings > About > Device Info > Clear User Data or Factory Reset. You may need to hold down a button on the screen to confirm, and you should feel a slight vibration when it's done and the Fitbit logo reappears on-screen. With the newest Fitbit Edge, it's even easier: swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings > Clear User Data.

Industry observers note that with older Fitbit trackers, you may have to connect the device to its charger and hold down a button or use a paperclip. With the Fitbit Flex, for example, which does not have a screen, connect the sensor to its charger, plug the charger into your computer via USB, find the black reset hole, and press it for three seconds with a paperclip. Wait for it to light up and confirm the reset.

Recent findings suggest that interestingly, the new screenless Fitbit Air (see our Fitbit Air review) does not have a traditional factory reset option. Instead, place it on its charger and press and hold the back button for 10 seconds (or until the status light flashes white). This will restart the device. If a new user pairs with the wearable, your account data will be cleared automatically.

Sources indicate that it's a good idea to manually unpair a Fitbit Air from your account first if you're handing it off. In the app, select the device from the top-left corner and, under System, select Disconnect & reset device. If it's not connecting to a newly introduced phone, forget it from your phone's Bluetooth menu (Settings > Bluetooth > tap the "i" beside the device and select Forget This Device.

According to recent reports, A factory reset is a last-resort option. I recently had issues syncing my Fitbit Edge with my iPhone; it got stuck in a boot loop and froze on a specific screen. Nothing I tried worked until I tried a factory reset.

In a recent development, it's notable to reiterate that a factory reset will erase all data that is stored locally on the device. This could include morning alarms, goals, notification settings, and any unsynced activities. It does not, however, delete data that's already been synced to the Google Health app. After resetting my Fitbit Edge, for example, all my daily data, including steps, workouts, and more, were still accessible in the app.

Sources indicate that if you're holding onto an older, discontinued Fitbit model and it's still working, look for instructions on how to factory reset it in the supporting documentation online, or check the Help menu in the Google Health app. Whichever model you have, once the factory reset process is done, it's like a newly introduced device again, and you can start the pairing and syncing process from scratch. Be patient: It may take some time to start accurately tracking your data again.

Google declined to take down Russell Brands not guilty prison message. Now its investigating.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, "So Russell has asked me to read something to you today," she stated.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This month, on Nov. 15, six days after Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for rape and sexual assault, Gallacher posted a video to his channel titled "The Good Work Continues" in which she read a message from him denying he had committed the crimes. The hour-long video drew more than 1 million views and prompted a takedown request from the Prison Service of England and Wales, which said the video could cause distress to Brand's victims.

According to recent reports, "So Russell has asked me to read something to you today," she stated. "Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support. As you know, I am not guilty for the offenses I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening.".

"I don't know which other men here are not guilty, and the ones that are, they are people that Christ died to save, like you and me," he added, according to his wife.

Google, which owns YouTube, initially turned down the request. On Nov. 18, the BBC reported that Google had declined because the video hadn't technically broken YouTube's rules. But by Nov. 19, Google had told the BBC it was looking into the video. "We’re aware of the newly introduced content and our teams are investigating," a spokesperson stated.

The company also pointed to its 2023 decision to suspend Brand's channel from the YouTube Partner Program, adding that the channel had been unable to earn money through YouTube since then. Google's statement gave no timeline for the review or details on what its teams were looking at, and the video was still up at time of publish (Nov. 21, 2 p.m. ET). There's another wrinkle to this story. The Ministry of Justice is investigating whether Brand broke prison rules by having his message made public. In England and Wales, prison rules generally restrict prisoners from discussing their own crimes in correspondence likely to be published or broadcast, with an exception for "serious representations about conviction or sentence.".

Justice Secretary Alex Norris called the broadcast "completely unacceptable" and remarked he expected action if Brand was found to have broken the rules.

Prison service guidance notes officials deciding whether to allow a broadcast should consider whether it could cause "serious distress" to victims, and The Guardian reported that the inquiry is weighing Brand's right to assert his innocence alongside questions about whether he sought permission and how soon the statement followed the verdict.

It has been revealed that mia Latter, who has publicly accused Brand of raping her at 16 and was not part of the trial, told the BBC that watching the video made her think about the women who testified. "I just again felt for those women that stood trial and everything they went through," she said.

British officials are still asking YouTube to take the video down. The Ministry of Justice still believes "YouTube should remove this content," but housing minister Matthew Pennycook told BBC Breakfast that the decision is "up to Google." Prime Minister Andy Burnham urged social media companies to "show some decency" and take the video down themselves, though saying he himself "wouldn't leap" to changing the law.

Labour MP and former safeguarding minister Jess Phillips, on the other hand, sees a case for a second Online Safety Act because, as she told BBC Radio 4, "we haven’t had prisoners who had massive YouTube followings." She cites how the current law requires platforms to tackle illegal content and protect children from harmful material; but, it doesn't specifically address what happens when someone outside prison shares a prisoner's message on social media.

Recent findings suggest that not everyone thinks the video should be taken down, though. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch added that she would first look at whether a law had been broken before pressing a private platform to remove the video. U.S. broadcaster Megyn Kelly went further, calling the reported push to deactivate Brand's channel one of Britain's "draconian free speech crackdowns.".

If the U.K. indeed writes a law in response to Brand's video, it’ll have to answer the more difficult question of how to decipher when a platform should step in to protect victims, or when there's a public interest in hearing what a prisoner has to say.
